items.prompt: Which part of a plant takes in water from the soil?

options.why: Leaves are up in the air. Their job is to make food using light.
The flower's job is to make seeds.
The stem carries water up the plant, but it does not take it from the soil.

hints: Think about which part touches the soil.
Water is in the soil, under the ground.
Picture a plant pulled out of a pot. Which part was in the soil?
items.explanation: The roots grow in the soil. They take in water and minerals and hold the plant in place.

items.prompt: Match each part of a plant to its job.
pairs: hold the plant in the soil and take in water
holds the plant up and carries water
hints: Each part has one main job.
Think about where each part is: under the ground, in the middle or at the top.
Start with the roots. What do they do in the soil?
items.explanation: Roots hold the plant and take in water, and the stem holds it up and carries water. Leaves use light to make food, and flowers make seeds.

items.prompt: The ___ holds a plant up and carries water to the leaves.
hints: This part is in the middle of the plant.
It joins the roots to the leaves, like a pipe.
The word starts with st.
items.explanation: The stem holds the plant up towards the light. Tiny tubes inside it carry water from the roots to the leaves.

items.prompt: Which part of the plant does each job? Sort the jobs.

items.text: take in water from the soil
hold the plant firmly in the ground
catch light with a wide, flat surface
use bright petals to attract insects

hints: Think about where each part is on the plant.
Jobs about soil belong to the part under the ground.
Start with make seeds. Which part grows seeds?
items.explanation: Roots work in the soil, holding the plant and taking in water. Leaves catch light to make food, and flowers attract insects and make seeds.

items.prompt: Many leaves are wide and flat. How does this help the plant?

options.text: It helps the leaves hold the plant in the soil.
options.why: Holding the plant in the soil is the job of the roots.

options.text: It helps the leaves store seeds.
options.why: Seeds are made in the flower, not in the leaves.

options.text: It helps the leaves carry water down to the roots.
options.why: Water travels up from the roots, not down from the leaves.

options.text: It helps the leaves catch lots of light to make food.

hints: Think about what leaves need to do their job.
Leaves make food. What do they need to catch for that?
Imagine holding a big flat sheet in the sunshine. What lands on it?
items.explanation: Leaves use light to make food for the plant. A wide, flat leaf has a big surface to catch lots of light.

items.prompt: A tree trunk is one of the four main plant parts. Which part is it?

options.why: Most roots are under the ground. The trunk stands above the ground.
Leaves grow from the branches. The trunk is thick and woody.
Flowers make seeds. The trunk holds the tree up.

hints: Think about what a trunk does for a tree.
Which part holds a plant up and carries water?
Compare a trunk with the green middle part of a small plant.
items.explanation: A trunk is a thick, woody stem. Like any stem, it holds the tree up and carries water from the roots to the leaves.

items.prompt: Dewi pulls a weed out of the ground. Long, thin threads hang from the bottom. What do they do?

options.why: These threads grow under the ground in the dark. Leaves make the food.

options.text: They take in water and hold the plant in the soil.
They make seeds for new plants.
options.why: Seeds are made in the flower.

options.text: They make the flowers smell nice.
options.why: Roots do not make smells for flowers. They work in the soil.

hints: Think about where the threads were growing.
These threads are a plant part you know.
Name the part that grows in the soil, then remember its jobs.
items.explanation: The threads are roots. Roots take in water and minerals from the soil and hold the plant firmly in the ground.

options.text: take in water from the soil

options.why: Leaves make food using light.
Flowers make seeds.

options.text: hold the plant in the ground

options.why: Bright flowers attract bees.

hints: Roots grow under the ground.
Cross out any job that needs light.
Think about what happens when you try to pull up a plant.
items.explanation: Roots take in water and minerals from the soil. They also spread out to hold the plant firmly in the ground.

items.prompt: Bees carry pollen from one flower to another. Why does the plant need this?

options.text: so the roots can take in more water
options.why: Pollen does not help the roots. Roots take in water by themselves.

options.text: so the leaves get more light
options.why: Bees do not change how much light the leaves get.

options.text: so the flower can make seeds

options.why: Pollen moves between flowers. It does not change the stem.

hints: Pollen moves between flowers, so think about the flower's job.
What does a flower make for new plants?
Look for the answer that is about the flower, not the other parts.
items.explanation: Pollen helps a flower make seeds. Bees carry pollen from flower to flower when they visit for nectar.

items.prompt: Caterpillars eat all the leaves on a chilli plant. Its roots and stem are fine. What will happen?

options.text: It grows faster because it is lighter.
options.why: Leaves make the plant's food. Without them, the plant cannot grow well.

options.text: Nothing changes, because the roots make the food.
options.why: Roots take in water and minerals. They do not make food.

options.text: The flowers start making all the food.
options.why: Flowers make seeds. Leaves are the main food makers.

options.text: It cannot make enough food, so it grows poorly.

hints: Which part of a plant makes its food?
Think about what the plant has lost.
Ask yourself: can the roots make food in the dark soil?
items.explanation: Leaves use light to make the plant's food. With no leaves, the plant cannot make enough food and grows poorly until new leaves grow.

items.prompt: A cactus has sharp spines and a thick green stem. It has no wide leaves. Which part makes most of its food?

options.why: Spines are thin and hard. They protect the cactus and help it lose less water.
Roots are in the dark soil. They take in water, not light.
A cactus flower makes seeds. It is not the main food maker.

hints: Food is made in green parts that get lots of light.
Spines are too thin to catch much light.
Look for the biggest green part of the cactus.
items.explanation: The thick green stem of a cactus catches light and makes food. Its spines are leaves that have changed shape to protect the plant and save water.

items.prompt: Draw a flowering plant. Label the roots, stem, leaves and flower.

criteria.label: Draws roots, a stem, leaves and a flower
Puts the roots under the ground line
Labels all four parts with lines

hints: Draw a line for the soil first.
Start with the roots under the line.
items.explanation: A flowering plant has roots in the soil, a stem, leaves and at least one flower. Clear labels with lines show each part.

items.prompt: Tap the part that uses sunlight to make food for the plant.

figure.alt: A plant growing in soil. It has a flower at the top, a long stem, one big leaf and roots under the ground.

hints: Plants make food using light from the Sun.
This part is flat and green.
It catches the light.
items.explanation: The leaves use sunlight, water and air to make food for the plant.

items.prompt: Label the parts of the plant. One label is not needed.

figure.alt: A plant growing in soil. It has a flower at the top, a long stem, one big leaf and roots under the ground.

hints: The part at the top that makes seeds is the flower.
The long part holds the plant up.
The part under the soil takes in water.
items.explanation: The labels are flower, leaf, stem and roots. A fruit is not drawn here.
